title: USP53 Regulates Proliferation and Apoptosis in Breast Cancer Cells
author: Meng, Chen, et al.
materials: The tissues were made into routine paraffin sections, which underwent deparaffination with xylene and ethanol, and antigen retrieval at boiling. Afterwards, 3% H2O2 was used to eliminate the peroxidase, and 1% BSA was used to block the non-specific antigen. Incubation with primary antibody against Ki-67 (1:50; cat. No. AF0198, Affinity, Cincinnati, OH, USA) was performed at 4 ℃ overnight, and that of secondary antibody labeled with HRP was executed at room temperature for 60 min. Subsequently, the sections interacted with DAB reagent, stained with hematoxylin, soaked with 1% hydrochloric acid/ethanol, dehydrated with ethanol and xylene, finally mounted with gum.

Immunofluorescence staining was applied for detection of USP53 and ZMYND11 location in cells. The cells were pre-seeded on glass sides, and fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde (Sinopharm Chemical Reagent Beijing Co., Ltd, Beijing, China) for 15 min, permeated with 0.1% triton-100 (Beyotime Institute of Biotechnology) for 30 min, and blocked with 1% bovine serum albumn (BSA) (Sangon, Shanghai, China) for 15 min. Subsequently, the cells were incubated with antibody against with USP53 (1:100; cat. No. H00054532-B01P) or ZMYND11 (1:100; cat. No. H00054532-B01P, Abnova, Taipei City, Taiwan) at 4 ℃ overnight, and incubated with secondary antibody conjugated with Alexa Fluor® 488 or 555 fluorescent dye (1:200; CST, Boston, MA, USA) for 60 min. Finally, the nuclei were stained with DAPI (Aladdin, Shanghai, China), and sides were mounted with anti-fading reagent (SolarBio). The images were acquired at 400× magnification.

steps.title: Download datasets and generate models
steps.instruction: Obtain all required transcriptomic and structural data from public repositories and online tools.

substeps.instruction: Download TCGA and GTEx RNA‑seq data for pan‑cancer and normal tissues from the UCSC XENA website (https://xenabrowser.net/datapages/).
Download GEO datasets GSE10810 and GSE42568 from the NCBI GEO database (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/).
Generate a 3‑D structural diagram of USP53 using the SWISS‑MODEL server (https://swissmodel.expasy.org/).
Access the GEPIA2 portal (http://gepia2.cancer-pku.cn/) for RNA‑seq data of 9 736 tumors and 8 587 normal tissues and install its Python package for visual analysis.
Use the Kaplan‑Meier Plotter (http://kmplot.com/) to retrieve USP53 expression and survival information from >30 000 samples across 21 cancers.

steps.title: Differential expression with Limma
steps.instruction: Identify down‑regulated USP family genes in breast cancer using the Limma package in R.

substeps.instruction: Load TCGA breast cancer and normal breast tissue expression data into R.
Run Limma to compare USP family member expression between tumor and normal samples.
For each dataset (GSE10810, GSE42568, TCGA, GEPIA2) screen genes with log2FC < -1 and adjusted p‑value (padj) < 0.05.
Intersect the four gene lists to obtain the final set of down‑regulated genes.

steps.title: USP53 expression across cancers
steps.instruction: Assess USP53 transcription levels and paired differences in multiple cancer types.

substeps.instruction: Query USP53 expression in the pan‑cancer database using GEPIA2 and the Kaplan‑Meier Plotter.
Use the Stats and Car R packages to compare USP53 expression between tumor and normal tissues for 33 cancers from TCGA and GTEx, including paired analyses.
Summarize the four analyses and intersect the results to define the cancer species where USP53 shows significant differences.

steps.title: USP53 gene correlation and enrichment
steps.instruction: Identify genes correlated with USP53 and perform functional enrichment.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Pearson correlation coefficients between USP53 and all other genes in breast cancer expression data.
Filter correlated genes with |Cor| > 0.5 and padj < 0.05.
Perform GO and KEGG enrichment of the filtered gene set using the ClusterProfiler R package.
Compute pairwise Jaccard similarity of enriched terms and conduct hierarchical clustering with the Hclust function.

steps.title: Diagnostic and survival analysis
steps.instruction: Evaluate USP53 as a diagnostic marker and its impact on patient survival.

substeps.instruction: Use the pROC R package to generate ROC curves and calculate AUC for USP53 in breast cancer diagnosis.
Employ the Kaplan‑Meier Plotter to compare overall survival between high‑ and low‑USP53 (or ZMYND11) expression groups.

steps.title: Visualize bioinformatics results
steps.instruction: Create figures summarizing the computational analyses.

substeps.instruction: Plot data visualizations with ggplot2.
Generate Venn diagrams of overlapping gene sets using the VennDiagram package.

steps.title: Culture breast cell lines
steps.instruction: Maintain immortalized mammary epithelial and breast cancer cell lines in appropriate media.

substeps.instruction: Obtain MCF‑12A, MCF‑7, T47D, BT474, SKBR3, MDA‑MB‑453, and MDA‑MB‑231 from iCell (Shanghai, China).
Culture MCF‑12A in the manufacturer‑provided special medium.
Culture MCF‑7, T47D, BT474, and SKBR3 in MEM (SolarBio, Beijing, China).
Culture MDA‑MB‑453 and MDA‑MB‑231 in L‑15 medium (Servicebio, Wuhan, Hubei, China).
Supplement MEM and L‑15 with 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin.
Incubate all cells at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ atmosphere.

steps.title: Transfect cells and select with G418
steps.instruction: Introduce USP53 overexpression or knockdown vectors and generate stable cell lines.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Lipofectamine™ 3000 (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA) reagent according to the manufacturer’s protocol and mix with plasmid DNA in serum‑free medium.
Add the transfection mixture to cells and incubate under standard culture conditions.
At 24 h post‑transfection, add G418 antibiotic: 500 µg ml⁻¹ for MCF‑7 cells and 600 µg ml⁻¹ for MDA‑MB‑231 cells (Biosharp Life Science, Hefei, Anhui, China).
Maintain selection for 1–2 weeks, then isolate single colonies and continue culture with the same G418 concentration for an additional 2 weeks.
Designate the surviving populations as USP53‑stably‑overexpressed or USP53‑silenced cells.

steps.title: Treat cells with synthesis inhibitors
steps.instruction: Block protein synthesis and degradation for functional assays.

substeps.instruction: Add cycloheximide (CHX) to a final concentration of 20 µg ml⁻¹ (Aladdin, Shanghai, China) to inhibit translation.
Add MG132 to a final concentration of 10 µM (Macklin Inc, Shanghai, China) to inhibit the proteasome.

steps.title: Immunohistochemistry staining
steps.instruction: Stain tissue sections for Ki‑67 and prepare slides for microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Section paraffin‑embedded tissues and deparaffinize sequentially with xylene and graded ethanol.
Perform antigen retrieval by boiling the slides in retrieval buffer.
Quench endogenous peroxidase with 3 % H₂O₂.
Block non‑specific binding with 1 % bovine serum albumin (BSA).
Incubate slides with primary anti‑Ki‑67 antibody (1:50; cat. No. AF0198, Affinity, Cincinnati, OH, USA) at 4 °C overnight.
Incubate with HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody at room temperature for 60 min.
Develop color with DAB substrate, counterstain with hematoxylin, then dip briefly in 1 % HCl/ethanol.
Dehydrate through graded ethanol, clear in xylene, and mount with mounting gum.

steps.title: Score USP53 IHC staining
steps.instruction: Quantify USP53 protein expression in stained sections.

substeps.instruction: Assign an intensity score: 1 (negative), 1 (weak), 2 (moderate), 3 (intense).
Multiply percentage and intensity scores; a total < 6 indicates low expression, > 7 indicates high expression.

steps.title: Prepare cells for cell‑cycle flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Fix, stain, and analyze DNA content to determine cell‑cycle distribution.

substeps.instruction: Collect cells and fix in 70 % ethanol at 4 °C overnight.
Wash cells with PBS.
Incubate with RNase A at 37 °C for 30 min.
Stain with propidium iodide (PI) in the dark for 30 min.
Acquire data on a flow cytometer (Agilent, Santa Clara, CA, USA) and calculate proliferative index as (G2 + S)/G1.

steps.title: Apoptosis flow cytometry assay
steps.instruction: Detect early and late apoptosis using Annexin V‑FITC/PI staining.

substeps.instruction: Incubate cells with Annexin V‑FITC at room temperature for 10 min in the dark.
Add PI and incubate for an additional 5 min (dark).
Immediately analyze samples on a flow cytometer.

steps.title: Immunofluorescence staining
steps.instruction: Visualize subcellular localization of USP53 and ZMYND11.

substeps.instruction: Seed cells on glass slides (sides).
Fix with 4 % paraformaldehyde (Sinopharm Chemical Reagent Beijing Co., Ltd) for 15 min.
Permeabilize with 0.1 % Triton‑X‑100 (Beyotime) for 30 min.
Block with 1 % BSA (Sangon, Shanghai, China) for 15 min.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibody against USP53 (1:100; cat. No. H00054532‑B01P) or ZMYND11 (1:100; cat. No. H00054532‑B01P, Abnova, Taipei City, Taiwan).
Incubate with Alexa Fluor® 488 or 555 secondary antibody (1:200; CST, Boston, MA, USA) for 60 min.
Stain nuclei with DAPI (Aladdin, Shanghai, China).
Mount slides with anti‑fading reagent (SolarBio).
Capture images at 400× magnification.

steps.title: Confirm USP53 modulation
steps.instruction: Validate overexpression or knockdown of USP53 at mRNA and protein levels.

substeps.instruction: Extract RNA from transfected cells and perform real‑time PCR to quantify USP53 mRNA.
Prepare protein lysates and run western blotting to detect USP53 protein.
Compare expression levels to control cells; confirm successful overexpression or silencing.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of data
steps.instruction: Analyze experimental results using appropriate statistical tests.

substeps.instruction: Present data as mean ± standard deviation (SD).
For two independent groups, use unpaired t‑test or Wilcoxon rank‑sum test (if non‑normal or heteroscedastic).
For paired groups, use paired t‑test or Wilcoxon signed‑rank test.
For > 2 groups, apply ANOVA or Kruskal‑Wallis test followed by Bonferroni’s multiple‑comparison correction.
Analyze IHC categorical data with chi‑square or Fisher’s exact test.
Consider p < 0.05 as statistically significant.
